          1.  Transmitted under separate cover is approximately fifteen
feet of moving picture film taken by Mr. Nicholas Mariana, of 2919
First Avenue North, Great Falls, Montana, who is general manager
of the Great Falls Baseball Club.

          2.  Mr. Mariana made these pictures on 15 August 1950 between
the hours of 11:25 and 11:30 A. M., at Great Falls, Montana.  On
interview, he stated that he first fighted the objects while standing
in the grandstand of the ball park located at 26th Street and Eleventh
Avenue North, Great Falls, Montana, and that he saw two bright disc
shaped objects proceeding in a southerly direction at an altitude
of approximately ten thousand feet and at a distance of about three-
quarters of a mile in a westerly direction, from the observer's view-
point.  Mr. Mariana then stated that he ran downstairs and outside
to his car from which he obtained his camera and made the pictures
shown in the film.  From the time of first sighting to the
completion of taking of the pictures, Mr. Mariana estimated con-
sumed approximately twenty seconds.  At the time of his taking
the pictures, a Miss Virginia Raunig, 112 Second Avenue North,
Great Falls, Montana, who is employed as his secretary, was a
witness.

          3.  The water tower in instant pictures is located approximately
seven hundred feet in a southwesterly direction from the point at
which Mr. Mariana stood when taking the pictures and the tower is
approximately one hundred seventy-five feet in height.

MEMORANDUM FOR:  Director of Naval Intelligence
                 Attention:  Op 322Y5

SUBJECT:  Interpretation of Movies of Unidentified Flying Objects

     1.  The attached movies (see Incl. 1) are possibly the best
documentary evidence yet obtained on unidentified flying objects.
They have been analyzed by an Air Force photographic laboratory.
However, it is our desire to obtain an independent analysis by a
separate laboratory in order that we may better interpret the
implications of these data.  For this reason, it is requested
that as complete an interpretation as possible be rendered by a
Navy activity.

     2.  Circumstances surrounding the photography are summarized
in Inclosure 2.  Additional details were requested by messages
which are included as Inclosures 3 and 5 and were obtained in the
replies attached as Inclosures 4 and 6.  With regard to Inclosures
5 and 6, the final footage of film referred to has been detached
and returned to CPO Newhouse.  However, it was deduced from this
portion that Newhouse obtained excellent results while hand-
holding the camera; there was almost no camera motion evident.
This deduction was applied to the analysis of that portion of the
film depicting the motion of the single object which detached itself

1.  Enclosure (1) is forwarded herewith for whatever value it may have in con-
nection with your investigation of the so-called "Flying Saucers".  Pertinent
data follows:

Place:     About 7 miles north of Tremonton, Utah on U.S. Highway No. 30S.

Time:      1110 Wednesday 2 July 1952.

Camera:    B&H Automaster, magazine load, 3" telephotolens, 16 frames per
           second.  Handheld.

Exposure:  First few feet - f:8.  Balance - f:16.  Clear sun, cloudless sky.
           EKCo Kodachrome film - Daylight.  Exposure was changed with the
           mistaken idea of darkening the sky to gain greater contrast.  The
           result was merely general under exposures.

General Background:  Driving from Washington, D.C. to Portland, Oregon, on
           the morning of 2 July my wife noticed a group of objects in the
           sky that she could not identify.  She asked me to stop the car and
           look.  There was a group of about ten or twelve objects - that bore
           no relation to anything I had seen before - milling about in a
           rought formation and proceeding in a westerly direction.  I opened
           the luggage compartment of the car and got my camera out of a suit-
           case.  Loading it hurriedly, I exposed approximately thirty feet of
           film.  There was no reference point in the sky and it was impossible
           for me to make any estimate of speed, size, altitude or distance.
           Toward the end one of the objects reversed course and proceeded away
           from the group.  I held the camera still and allowed this single
           one to cross the field of view, picking it up again and repeating
           for three or four such passes.  By this time all of the objects
           had disappeared.  I expended the balance of the film late that
           afternoon on a mountain somewhere in Idaho.

SUGGESTED POINTS FOR ANALYSIS

                    SECURITY INFORMATION
     The following questions are suggested for guidance regarding the
general type of analysis desired:

     1.  Are images made by light source or reflection?

     2.  Any indication of what kind of objects could have caused images?
Is there any bird sufficiently actinic to cause images?  Could they have
been caused by aircraft or balloons?

     3.  What causes impression that some objects at times appear to
become 2 or 3 where there was originally one; or, conversely, 2 or 3 objects
at times appear to merge into one.

     4.  Do all objects have same characteristics?

          a.  Same apparent shape?
          b.  Same Color?
          c.  Same relative size?
          d.  Same general motion?

     5.  What are shape(s), color(s) and relative size(s) of objects?

     6.  To what can the "fade-in" and "fade-out" of the objects be attributed?

     7.  What type motion is attributable to the objects about their own axis
as well as about axis of flight path)?

     8.  Is there any accelleration evident in their motion along light
path axis?

     9.  Can the motion of the camera (panning and joggling) be allowed
for sufficiently to permit determination of the angular velosity of objects
which cross the field of view?  (Reference particularly the single object
which crosses field; photographer states that camera was held motionless
while object crossed field of view.)

     10.  Determine patterns of flight from position plots for each

frame, then:

          a.  Is there any recurring pattern in the relative position
              of the objects?

              any maneuvers, particularly violent maneuvers?
          c.  Is relative position maintained coincidental with movement

Dear Mr. Gorman:

     Your letter of 29 October 1952 to the President has been referred
to the USAF since, within the Department of Defense, the USAF has
primary interest in investigation of "flying saucer" reports. It is
gratifying to receive such expression of interest from public-minded
individuals. In your case, we are grateful for the opportunity to
correct a misapprehension.

     The USAF has not prepared any recent report arriving at any con-
clusions with respect to the existence or nonexistence of "flying
saucers". It is believed that Mr. Robert S. Allen, in his article
of September 26, referred to a report prepared for public release by
a private group of civilians. In commenting on this, the USAF stated
that the report reflected the conclusions of individuals who were in
no way connected with the Air Force. We take this opportunity to
reiterate this to you.

     It is true that the statements of Mr. DesVergers were startling;
however, a thorough investigation of the incident has been conducted
and it has been determined that the sensational aspects of the orig-
inal stories carried by the national press agencies were exaggerated.
Further, the USAF made no attempt to restrict Mr. DesVergers' discus-
sion or personal exploitation of the alleged incident; this he admitted
in an Associated Press dispatch datelined West Palm Beach, Florida,
August 27, 1952.

     The Air Force is actively interested in the investigation of
"flying saucer" incidents. No facts have been withheld from the
public. The investigators hope to reach some conclusions concerning
the existence and source of the objects. To date, sufficient evidence
is not available to support any firm conclusions. I am confident that
when scientific analysis of available evidence supports a conclusion,
the public will be duly informed.

     It is sincerely hoped that these comments will allay your concern
on this subject. The manner in which you have sought an answer to

                              October 29, 1952


President Harry Truman
White House
Washington, D. C.

Dear Mr.. President:

        Permit me to take the liberty of writing you on
"flying saucers".

        It is becoming generally known that the Air Force
has a report concluding that flying saucers originate from
sources outside this planet. Articles like that of Robert
S. Allen, dated Sept. 26th are being photostated and circulated
privately. The statements of Mr. DesVergers of West Palm
Beach, Florida, concerning his flying saucer experience and
what he was told by the military and other incidents have
convinced many including myself that the "saucers" are real
and interplanetary.

        I think it is unfortunate that a matter which is
of such great import must be investigated privately by citizens
who would like to and should be permitted to cooperate with
and analyze with their government and military authorities.
I think people who are afraid to tell the people of the
possibilities of the flying saucers should bolster their
faith in the people of this country and democracy.

        I hope you unveil the secrecy of the air force
report. I also hope you decide that this is not a matter of
military secrecy and that events concerning flying saucers
be made available to the public as they unfold.


                         Very truly yours,



                         Robert J. Gorman

     1.  The file on the sighting at Austin, Texas on 8 June 52, previously borrowed
from ATIAA-5, is returned herewith.

     2.  The Photographic Division, AFCAG, made a set of color duplicates (enlarged)
which is attached for your retention (Incl 3).  Black and white reproductions pre-
viously attached to the file are also included in Incl 3.  In addition, the
Photographic Division made a number of black and white enlargements which are
attached for your retention (Incl 4).

     3.  Based on further analysis, the Photographic Division and this office do not
agree with the WADC evaluation of parhelions ("sun dogs") since the images do not
appear at the required angle of 22° or 46° nor are they in line horizontally with
the sun as would be required for the formation of a parhelion (which would appear at
the intersection of the inner or outer halo circles - 22° and 46° respectively -
with the parhelic circle; the latter is in a horizontal plane coincidental with the
position of the sun).  Additionally, it will be noted in the photographs that the
images display a flat portion which appears inverted from the corresponding portion
of the sun behind the cloud.  Since a parhelion is the result of refraction through
ice crystals, the resulting image would not be inverted.  Instead, it is our opinion
that the images are possibly a form of mirage caused by a hot air mass which
traveled from left to right across the field of view and acted as a lens.  However,
there is a small image in the third photograph of the sequence which, if evaluated
as another image of the same type, would seemingly eliminate both parhelia and
mirages from consideration.  This image is located directly above the seventh
telephone pole from the right at a vertical distance approximately equal to the
height of the pole.  The minute size of this image militates strongly against the
mirage theory since the hot air mass would have had to turn about 90° and proceed
away from the camera in order to produce this effect.  Therefore, further analysis
appears to be justified.  Suggest the consultant astronomer be asked for an opinion.

     4.  Recommend that the original photographs (Incl 2) be returned to the owner
immediately as requested in the report covering this incident.

Mr. Leon Davidson
804 South Irving Street
Arlington 4, Virginia

Dear Mr. Davidson:

     The Air Force Press Desk, Office of Public Information,
Department of Defense, has advised my office of your continued
interest in reports of unusual observations of aerial objects.
Your previous correspondence concerning this matter has been
reviewed and we believe that your requests for additional
information cannot be adequately treated by correspondence.

     May I advise you that we are aware of the responsible
position you hold and of the security clearance that has
been granted you in your present capacity.

     We would appreciate an opportunity to discuss your views
concerning possible sources of these objects with you on a
personal basis. Ofcourse the matter will be treated in complete
confidence. Unfortunately the officer most cognizant of our
investigations in this field will be out of town until after 1
November. If you will contact my office, Liberty 5-6700,
extension 74072, on or after 3 November we will be happy to
arrange a meeting with you at sometime mutually convenient.

Mr. Nicholas Mariana
3235 Fifth Avenue South
Great Falls, Montana

Dear Mr. Mariana:

     You are probably aware of the fact that the Air Force
is still continuing the investigation and analysis of "flying
saucers". We are presently attempting to make a comparative
analysis of recent sightings against those made in previous
years. In this connection, the report of a sighting made by
you on 15 August 1950 has aroused our interest. Unfortunately,
however, our duplicate copy of the movies which you took of
these objects has been inadvertently misplaced.

     Therefore, we would be most grateful if you would
permit us to borrow your original movies for study and dup-
lication. In so doing you would be rendering us a great
service.

     We will have an officer from Great Falls Air Force
Base contact you about 22 October and, should you consider
our request favorably, he will obtain the movies and give
you a receipt for them. We will then return them as soon
as possible thereafter.

     Your cooperation and consideration in this matter is
earnestly solicited!

                                    Sincerely,

Dear Mr. Varela:

     We acknowledge, with sincere thanks, the kind offers made
on behalf of your group in your letter of 28 August 1952.  It
is indeed gratifying to see the cooperation extended the Air
Force by organizations such as yours in our attempt to evolve
a final solution to the unidentified flying objects problem.

     Since the Air Technical Intelligence Center at Wright-
Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio is the activity which is respon-
sible for the investigation and analysis of these reports, we
are forwarding your letter to them.  For the same reason, we
would like to suggest that you forward all data and findings
directly to them rather than to this Headquarters.  In this
manner, the information which you supply will be incorporated
into the program much more quickly.

     You will probably hear from the Center in the near future.

Mr. John J. Phillips
6047 Baldwin Avenue
Temple City, California

Dear Mr. Phillips:

     The Secretary of the Army has referred your letter of 29 August
1952 to us for attention.  Although we had already processed yours of
26 August to us, we were, nonetheless, very happy to receive your
additional comments.

     We would like to assure you that the Air Force is not treating
the "flying saucer" situation lightly.  As recently announced, we are
conducting a very serious program of intelligence investigation and
analysis, and we will continue to give the problem adequate but not
frantic attention.  By this time you have most probably received a
very detailed questionnaire from the Air Technical Intelligence Center
with a request to enter as much detail as you are able to recall about
the object which you observed.  This should indicate to you our earnest
efforts to find a satisfactory solution to the problem.

     We hope that these brief comments have served to reassure you of
the Air Force's attitude towards this subject.  We appreciate your
keen interest and efforts to assist us.

          x095. Phillips, Sincerely, John

     We have received your letter of 4 September 1952 with the

     In order to relieve you of any further worry about the
newspaper photographs, we can assure you that they are fakes.

satire. Unfortunately, however, many such attempts at humor

one of these instances.

hope that our comments have reassured you.

27TH Air Div (Def), Norton AFB, Cal                    PAGE  1  OF  1  PAGES

                                                    #506502

Statement:

     On the 19 August 1952, at approximately 2000 PDST, Algiers took control of
Swanee Red from Conform at georef position DD 1050, at which time he was given a
vector of 290°.

     Swanee Red Leader then called Algiers stating that he was steady on 290° and
that he had a stranger at one o'clock.  Algiers asked if he could tell what type
of aircraft it was?  Swanee Red Leader gave a negative reply, but Swanee Red 2
said it could possibly be a Big Photo because it appeared as a large type aircraft.
Algiers then instructed Swanee Red to investigate the stranger, also that Algiers
had no contact on the stranger as it was in our clutter area, in the vicinity of
San Gorgonio Mountain.

     Lt. Otis, Swanee Red Leader, then reported that upon turning into the
stranger, it appeared to have no tail assembly and showed great acceleration in
moving away from them in an easterly direction and disappearing into space.

     Algiers did not make radar pick-up on the unusual sighting at any time.

     Lt. Otis called the controller, (Captain Borgeson), at Algiers after landing
and described the object as oval at the base and tapered toa heavy center section;
he also re-affirmed that it did not have a tail section.



                              RALPH P. BORGESON
                              Captain     USAF
                              Chief Director

Dear Mr. Reiley:

     Since Air Force Intelligence is responsible for the in-
vestigation and analysis of unidentified flying objects,
General Vandenberg has referred your letter of 14 September
1952 to us and requested that we answer your questions.

     Although our analysis of the many sightings which occurred
on the night of 12 September is not yet complete, we have
tentatively concluded that the object was a meteor.  It will
be quite some time before our final analysis is available
since much checking and study of the various reports is required.

     In reply to your query "Are we being invaded", we are
inclosing a standard release which gives in some detail our

objects plus many other things about which we have been
queried often in the recent past.  We trust that it will answer
your question satisfactorily and assist you in answering any
other questions which you may have or may receive from your
readers.

proper answers directly from us.

     1.  The inclosed report, prepared by Capt. Dale L. Leavitt of the National
Guard, was obtained from the National Guard Bureau, Washington.  It concerns
the sighting of an unidentified flying object which allegedly landed in the
vicinity of Flat Woods, West Virginia around 1930 EST 12 Sept 52, and the alleged
observation of a "monster" shortly thereafter in the area in which the flying
object supposedly landed, (see Incls 1 and 2).

     2.  Prior to receipt of the inclosed, the only information received on this
incident was through the press.  The Washington DAILY NEWS advised OSD-OPI of
certain information which they had obtained from persons in the locale.  One
comment, attributed to Capt. Leavitt, was that the "skid marks" along the side of
the hill were formed by a greasy deposit which felt like graphite.  This appeared
to bear a possible relation to the incident of the "perfect circle" in Arlington,
Virginia on 2 Sept 52.  Therefore, Capt. Leavitt was contacted and confirmed this
statement.  He was requested to obtain soil and vegetation samples and submit
them to this office.

     3.  Samples arrived 29 Sept 52 and show no evidence of a graphite-like deposit.
They are attached as Incl 3 for your disposition.

     4.  Some of the principals in this incident were on the TV program "We The
People" on 19 Sept 52.  During this program a drawing was shown which was claimed
to represent a composite of the descriptions of all witnesses.  A rough sketch
was made of this drawing and is attached as Incl. 4.  It is vaguely reminiscent of
a character which appeared in a comic strip a few years ago.

     5.  All inclosures are for your retention.

Dear Misses Neuwirth and Schilling:

     Your letter of 15 September 1952 was referred to us by the National
Security Council.  As they told you in their letter of 17 September 1952,
we are responsible for the "flying saucer" investigation.

     With regard to your questions about "flying saucer" reports, we
are inclosing a standard release which sets forth the official Air Force
attitude and philosophy on the subject.  We hope that it will answer your
questions satisfactorily.

     The only report we have received of a "fire-breathing monster"
allegedly seen in West Virginia has been through the press.  Because
this observation was made at night and under conditions of excitement
and, furthermore, since the story has died a natural death without
further mention in the press, we discount it entirely.  It has been noted
in the past that a flurry of "flying saucer" reports will stimulate the
imagination and give rise to many complementary reports evolved through
association.  We are convinved that the report from West Virginia
represents just such a case where the necessary stimulus was provided
by the meteor sighting reports of the preceding Friday night.

     We hope that these brief comments have provided satisfactory answers
to your questions.

Maj. Gen. John Samford,
Headquarters G-2, Air Force,
Department of Defense,
Washington 25, D. C.

Dear Sir:-

        Regarding the recent reports of the so called flying saucers, I am quite
sure that the hoax will be exposed by telling you that this is nothing more than
the silver iodide used in artificial rainmaking.  This is especially true if the
silver iodide came in contact with radioactive clouds or so called thunderclouds.

        The solution of this hoax is quite simple, if you will check your records
you will find that flying saucers were first seen about the time when silver
iodide came into usage for artificial rainmaking.  Again, silver is a reflective
agency and will reflect all types of light, which accounts for the various hues
reported by sky gazers.  Again, silver iodide, if radioactive or ionized by an
electrical cloud will be come fluorescent, which accounts for flyers being unable
to overtake the so called flying saucers, and their habit of disappearing.

        Of course, we must eliminate such reports of flying saucers as were accountable
by balloons, foo-fighters, meteorites, and the person who just calls up a newspaper
with the hope of getting his name in the papers.  Also to be disqualified are such
reports as to ascertain that they are interplanetary space ships.  If it were at
all possible for another planet to send aircraft of any type to our atmosphere,
it would simply burn up the same as a meteorite and such space ship remains would
be found the same as meteorites.  As far as I know, no such wreckage has ever been
found.


                                        Respectfully yours,

     Major General James A. Samford
     Chief of Intelligence
     Pentagon Building
     Arlington, Virginia

     Dear Sir:

          In connection with "flying saucer" newspaper accounts of
     observations on the search radar system at the Washington
     National Airport, it occurred to me that the described be-
     havior could possibly be accounted for in the following manner:

     High power, narrow beam fire control radar systems of the usual
     type might conceivably, under unusual atmospheric conditions,
     create enough ionization along points on the beam in the upper
     atmosphere to allow the return of an appreciable echo to the
     search radar system from such points.  The apparent motion would
     be quite haphazard, following whatever the fire control radar
     operator does in directing the beam.

     This hypothesis is unattractive for several reasons:  Firstly,
     the power required for such an effect is many times greater
     than that put out by the usual radar.  Secondly, such echoes
     would presumably come from ionospheric heights and therefore
     could not appear at ranges of a few miles from the search radar,
     as was reported.  Thirdly, it seems unlikely that a coincident
     visual effect of any conspicuous magnitude would be produced.

     In spite of this, I am offering this suggestion in the belief
     that if considerable time, money and effort is being devoted to
     this problem, it might be worthwhile trying the relatively simple
     experiment of having a powerful fire control radar sweep out
     certain simple patterns to see if they can be detected on the
     search radar system, preferably at a time when "flying saucer"
     echoes are being observed.

                                        Very truly yours,

                                        s/
                                        John M. Hollywood
                                        Engineer

                                                August 2, 1952


          Maj. Gen. John A. Samford
          Air Force Director of Intelligence
          Washington, D. C.

          Dear Sir:

               I should like to present to you what I believe to
          be a tenable theory as to the origin and nature of the
          phenomena popularly known as "flying saucers".

               It has been amply demonstrated that electro-magnetic
          radiation of sufficient power density is capable of
          ionizing gas at low pressure.  Upon deionization, the
          gas emits radiation of characteristic wave lengths, some
          of which lie in the visible spectrum.  Further, it is
          known that radar equipment can detect ionized gas, such as
          northern lights, or charged water droplets, such as appear
          in thunderclouds.

               I believe that ionization of disc-shaped segments of
          air in the upper atmosphere may be caused by beams from a r
          radar transmitter held in a fixed position or slowly traversed, i
          instead of the usual sweeping motion.

               To verify the possibility, I propose in the very near
          future to conduct an experiment.  A glass sphere containing
          air at atmosphere pressure will be exposed to radiation of a
          known wave length and power density.  The pressure in the
          sphere will then be reduced until ionization occurs.  The
          screen of a separate radar transmitter-receiver will also
          be observed to note whether the change in the condition of
          the air is detectable by radar.

                                            Very truly yours,

                                            s/
                                            John C. Weber
                                            Assoc. Prof. of E. E.

                        MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

PROBLEM

     1.  To prepare DF to ATIC and non-military letters to Prof. John C.
Weber, Mr. John M. Hollywood and Mr. G. Francis Nauheimer.

FACTS AND DISCUSSION

     2.  In letters addressed to General Samford, the above-named gentlemen
offer theories as to the cause of aerial phenomean which they believe may
account for unidentified flying object sightings.  It is noteworthy that
Prof. Weber is Associate Professor of Electrical Engineering at the University
of Wisconsin, Mr. Hollywood is an engineer for the CBS Laboratories, and Mr.
Nauheimer is Director of the Glare Research Institute.

     3.  Since the proposals of Prof. Weber and Mr. Hollywood coincide
rather closely with the experiments of Mr. Scott of the Engineer Research
and Development Lab at Fort Belvoir as well as with the ideas of Dr. Possony,
their letters have been reviewed very carefully.  Copies are being maintained
here for further study.

     4.  Original letters received from Prof. Weber and Mr. Hollywood will
be forwarded to ATIC by DF after signature by D/I of replies.

     5.  Replies to the three gentlemen are attached.  They have been written
in the first person from General Samford.

     6.  Subject matter is not considered suitable for inclusion in the Daily
Staff Digest.

ACTION RECOMMENDED

     7.  Because of the professional status of the three correspondents,
it is strongly recommended that General Samford sign the attached replies.

MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

PROBLEM

1. To submit a Staff Study for coordination and approval.

FACTS AND DISCUSSION

2. It has become increasingly apparent over the past few months that certain revisions are required in JANAP 146(B), Communications Instructions for Reporting Vital Intelligence Sightings while Airborne (CIRVIS).

3. For some time there has existed quite a bit of confusion over the responsibility for evaluating CIRVIS reports, particularly the responsibility of this Headquarters. It has been noticed that very few evaluations have been made by field commands and that this Headquarters has been attempting to furnish ADC the required evaluations. However, these efforts are limited in that the information necessary for an evaluation is normally not readily available here, resulting in an inordinate time loss or, more frequently, the transmittal of an evaluation message which states that no further information is available here.

4. Additionally, the number of reports of unidentified flying objects which have been received over CIRVIS channels during the cyclic flurries of such sightings has given rise to some concern that CIRVIS communication channels may at some time be saturated, thereby providing an excellent opportunity for concealing an air attack which may be mounted against this country.

5. The fact that CIRVIS was restricted to airborne reports was also believed questionable.

6. These factors warranted the preparation of a staff study to examine objectively and completely the adequacy of JANAP 146 (B). Since certain aspects of unidentified flying objects reporting are inseparably related to CIRVIS, the study required the inclusion of this subject as well.

7. The attached study was prepared for this purpose and is believed to represent a thorough and objective analysis.

RESULTS OF EXAMINATION

          In answer to your specific inquiry, you are advised that the areas
     surrounding the three burned holes in the cap were examined for any residues
     which might indicate the nature of the incendiary material causing the burns,
     but no such residues were found.  Tests conducted on the sweatband of Q1
     indicate that the residue from a glowing ember used to burn a hole in the cloth
     was easily dislodged and removed by handling and "roughing" the burned area.

          Some observations made during the examination of Q1 may be of interest
     to you.  The major portion of the top side of the cap bill as well as the area
     surrounding the yellow and black emblem or insigne and the insigne itself have
     been subjected to the singeing action of a flame.  It is of interest to note
     that the singeing on these areas is not at all uniform as might be expected
     if the cap had been subjected to a single shot of a "red blob" of a fire of
     some kind.  The fact that the front edge of the cap bill is more severely
     scorched or singed than other portions of the cap suggests that the singeing
     could not have taken place when Mr. D. S. Desvergers was fired upon from a
     position almost vertically above him.  When the cap is observed from the front
     and left edge of the insigne and the fold in the blue cloth in the surrounding

Dear Sir:-

        Regarding the recent reports of the so called flying saucers, I am quite
sure that the hoax will be exposed by telling you that this is nothing more than
the silver iodide used in artificial rainmaking. This is especially true if the
silver iodide came in contact with radioactive clouds or so called thunderclouds.

        The solution of this hoax is quite simple, if you will check your records
you will find that flying saucers were first seen about the time when silver
iodide came into usage for artificial rainmaking. Again, silver is a reflective
agency and will reflect all types of light, which accounts for the various hues
reported by sky gazers. Again, silver iodide, if radioactive or ionized by an
electrical cloud will be come fluorescent, which accounts for flyers being unable
to overtake the so called flying saucers, and their habit of disappearing.

        Of course, we must eliminate such reports of flying saucers as were accountable
by balloons, foo-fighters, meteorites, and the person who just calls up a newspaper
with the hope of getting his name in the papers. Also to be disqualified are such
reports as to ascertain that they are interplanetary space ships. If it were at
all possible for another planet to send aircraft of any type to our atmosphere,
it would simply burn up the same as a meteorite and such space ship remains would
be found the same as meteorites. As far as I know, no such wreckage has ever been
found.

     Major General James A. Samford
     Chief of Intelligence
     Pentagon Building
     Arlington, Virginia

     Dear Sir:

          In connection with "flying saucer" newspaper accounts of
     observations on the search radar system at the Washington
     National Airport, it occurred to me that the described be-
     havior could possibly be accounted for in the following manner:

     High power, narrow beam fire control radar systems of the usual
     type might conceivably, under unusual atmospheric conditions,
     create enough ionisation along points on the beam in the upper
     atmosphere to allow the return of an appreciable echo to the
     search radar system from such points.  The apparent motion would
     be quite haphazard, following whatever the fire control radar
     operator does in directing the beam.

     This hypothesis is unattractive for several reasons:  Firstly,
     the power required for such an effect is many times greater
     than that put out by the usual radar.  Secondly, such echoes
     would presumably come from ionospheric heights and therefore
     could not appear at ranges of a few miles from the search radar,
     as was reported.  Thirdly, it seems unlikely that a coincident
     visual effect of any conspicuous magnitude would be produced.

     In spite of this, I am offering this suggestion in the belief
     that if considerable time, money and effort is being devoted to
     this problem, it might be worthwhile trying the relatively simple
     experiment of having a powerful fire control radar sweep out
     certain simple patterns to see if they can be detected on the
     search radar system, preferably at a time when "flying saucer"
     echoes are being observed.

                                        Very truly yours,

                                        s/
                                        John M. Hollywood

            Maj. Gen. John A. Samford
            Air Force Director of Intelligence
            Washington, D. C.

            Dear Sir:

                    I should like to present to you what I believe to
            be a tenable theory as to the origin and nature of the
            phenomena popularly known as "flying saucers".

                    It has been amply demonstrated that electro-magnetic
            radiation of sufficient power density is capable of
            ionizing gas at low pressure. Upon deionization, the
            gas emits radiation of characteristic wave lengths, some
            of which lie in the visible spectrum. Further, it is
            known that radar equipment can detect ionized gas, such as
            northern lights, or charged water droplets, such as appear
            in thunderclouds.

                    I believe that ionization of disc-shaped segments of
            air in the upper atmosphere may be caused by beams from a r
            radar transmitter held in a fixed position or slowly traversed, i
            instead of the usual sweeping motion.

                    To verify the possibility, I propose in the very near
            future to conduct an experiment. A glass sphere containing
            air at atmosphere pressure will be exposed to radiation of a
            known wave length and power density. The pressure in the
            sphere will then be reduced until ionization occurs. The
            screen of a separate radar transmitter-receiver will also
            be observed to note whether the change in the condition of
            the air is detectable by radar.

                                                Very truly yours,

                                                    s/
                                                John C. Weber
                                                Assoc. Prof. of E. E.

MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

PROBLEM:

1. To prepare non-military letter to Mrs. Nellie T. Dull of Staunton,
Virginia.

FACTS AND DISCUSSION:

2. On 1 Aug 52 Mrs. Dull wrote in a letter to USAF Intelligence in
which she theorized, in a completely amateurish manner, that electro-
magnetism could account for "flying saucers". There was absolutely no
technical foundation to her ideas, and, actually, she presented the entire
thing in the form of a question, viz. "please let me know if this is the
answer."

3. A routine reply, thanking her for the suggestion, was dispatched
by this office 20 August 1952.

4. In a second letter dated 12 Aug 52, Mrs. Dull expresses concern
that her ideas were "stolen" by Mr. Noel Scott of the Engineer Research
and Development Lab since the latter announced his ionization theory
shortly after Mrs. Dull wrote her first letter.

5. Copies of both letters from Mrs. Dull and our reply are
attached.

6. A reply has been prepared, the contents of which should alleviate
Mrs. Dull's concern.

7. Subject matter is not considered suitable for inclusion in the
Daily Staff Digest.

8. Approval, signature and dispatch of attached letter.

MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

PROBLEM:

1. To prepare a non-military letter to Mr. E. L. Lull of Salt
Lake City.

FACTS AND DISCUSSION:

2. In a telegram to this Directorate dated 29 July 1952 (AF IN
14051), Mr. Lull states that, based on certain recent data, his
calculations in his book "Daniel and the Atomic Equations of the
Loaves" may be in error by about 2 years.

3. A copy of this book was obtained through the Army Library
from the Library of Congress. It is significant that the latter
classifies the book as BS (Bible).

4. This analyst must plead innocent to any accusation that he
is a theologian. Nonetheless, on the assumption that any infor-
mation regardless of origin or nature may possibly prove helpful
to Intelligence and applying amateur theology, the book was
scanned and the following conclusions derived:

 a. Mr. Lull, who is an engineer, has attempted to
establish a correlation between certain significant dates in history
and specific passages in the Testaments and the Book of Mormon
by the use of mathematical analyses.

 b. Further, by the same analyses, he arrives at certain
future dates which, by analogy, he concludes are indicative of
extreme significance to the world. One such date is 4 Oct 54. It
is implied that a revelation will be made on that date in fulfillment
of one of Daniel's prophecies in the old Testament and that this
revelation will be a joyous rather than a grievous one.

5. It is assumed that Mr. Lull's statement to the effect that his
calculations may be in error by about 2 years refers to the 4 Oct 54
derivation and, further, that the error is positive, i.e. that the date

SECURITY INFORMATION

should be 4 Oct 52. This assumption is based on the urgency with
which Mr. Lull informed us of his error (by telegram).

6. It is additionally assumed that Mr. Lull intends that the
aforementioned date be associated with Project Blue Book since:

        a. He states in his telegram that the basis for his belief
that he made an error in his original calculations (presumably re
4 Oct 54) is "the recent hyperspace demonstrations of the Disc Company
in free space".

        b. His telegram was dispatched at the height of the most
recent "flying saucer" flurry in the press (the date of the telegram is
the same as that on which General Samford held a press conference on
the subject).

7. Accordingly, a reply to Mr. Lull has been prepared expressing
appreciation and stating that due notice has been taken of his con-
clusions.

8. Additionally, this analyst has marked 4 Oct down as a red letter
day and is eagerly awaiting its arrival since it apparently means that
the mystery of the "flying saucers" will finally be solved and his toil
towards that end will no longer be necessary.

9. Subject matter is not considered suitable for inclusion in the
Daily Staff Digest.

ACTION RECOMMENDED:

10. Approval and dispatch of attached letter to Mr. Lull.

     1.  The inclosures relate to the investigation of an incident which allegedly
occurred during the night of 1/2 September 1952, and which has a possible relation
to Project Blue Book.  The investigation was conducted by this office on 3 and
4 September 1952.

     2.  Inclosures 1 and 2 give details of the investigation.  A list of samples
obtained during the investigation and pertinent data on each are included in
Inclosure 3.  These samples have been forwarded to OSI with a request that they
be submitted to the FBI for lab analysis.  The results of the analysis will be
forwarded as soon as they become available.

     3.  Inclosure 4 contains 5 photographic negatives taken of the area in
question at 1430 hours on 4 September 1952.  All shots except the one showing
the cap on the ground were taken of the ring in its original state.  The color
of the deposit was approximately the same as on the preceding evening when
samples were taken, but the amount of the deposit appeared to have diminished
somewhat.  The shot in which the cap appears on the ground was taken after lime-
stone had been spread over the original ring in order to provide better definition.
Care was taken to duplicate the original configuration, both as to shape and density.

SUMMARY OF CIRCUMSTANCES: INVESTIGATION OF POSSIBLE
UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECT - ARLINGTON, VIRGINIA
1-2 September 1952


1. At 1600 hours on 3 Sep 52, the Directorate of Intelligence,
Hq., USAF received a telephone call from Mr. Walter Storm, 227 18th
Street, SE, Washington, D.C. (phone LI 31298) that an unusual circle
was found marked on the lawn of his father, Mr. Charles Walter Storm,
on the morning of 2 Sep 52 and that he believed it might bear some
relation to the USAF investigation of unidentified flying objects.

2. Major Fournet, of the D/I, called on the elder Mr. Storm at
his residence (102 North Garfield Street, Arlington, Va., phone:
CH 8508) during the evening of 3 Sep 52.

3. The following was found on Mr. Storm's rear lawn (refer to
sketch in Incl 2):

     a. A circle 18 feet in diameter and nearly perfectly formed
was marked on the lawn by a deposit of some unknown gray substance
which was adhering to the grass in clusters of fine globules.

     b. The band of the circle (around the periphery) was an average
of approximately 6 inches wide.

     c. The deposits in the band were less pronounced and sometimes
absent for short distances where depressions or uneveness in the ground
surface occurred.

     d. A small evergreen bush was located at a point about 40 inches
inside the circle and did not appear to have been disturbed in any way nor
were any deposits present on or around it.

     e. A clothes line frame located on a central pole overhung the
circle somewhat and had been in place (approximately as shown in Incl 2)
on the night in question.

     f. An antenna wire about 40 feet above the ground overhung the
circle, exact amount undetermined.

     g. No other vegetation in the area contained any deposits or
marks (small trees were present, as close as 6 or 8 feet from the circle).

     h. Three types of fertilizer were stored in covered drums near
the garage about 15 feet away from the circle.

     4.  Mr. and Mrs.Storm were interviewed and offered the following
information:

          a.  Mr. Storm cut the grass in the area in question around
1800-1900 hours on 1 Sep 52.  The clippings were left where they fell.

          b.  At 2300 hours on 1 Sep 52, Mr. Storm put his dog in the
basement for the night.  (Note:  the dog barks at anyone who comes into
the yard, and, until that time had not sounded off).

          c.  (As related to Mr. Storm later by Mrs. Whitehurst, a neighbor
immediately in the rear of the Storm residence and adjacent to the lawn in
question.)  Mrs. Whitehurst was awakened at about 0400 hours on 2 Sep 52
by barking of dog "which seemed to be in distress".  She looked out of a
window in the rear of her house but failed to see anything (it was a rather
dark night).

          d.  Upon going out to his car at 0730 hours 2 Sep 52, Mr. Storm
noticed the circle and walked over to examine it.  He describes it as
having at that time a brown, oily-sandy appearance with what seemed to
be a very fine granular structure (as though a fine sand mixed with light
oil had been spread to form this ring).  He rubbed some of the substance
between his fingers and found it faintly gritty and definitely oily.  Mrs.
Storm corroborates this description.

          e.  During mid-afternoon of 2 Sep 52 Mrs. Storm reexamined the ring
and found that the color had changed to grayish-blue, and it no longer
appeared to be oily.  However it still felt oily but no longer felt gritty.
She detected no odor upon smelling it.

          f.  Upon returning from work at 1700 hours 2 Sep 52, Mr. Storm
again examined it with his wife.  He describes the color as purplish-gray;
Mrs. Storm describes the color as bluish-gray.  Both agree that the
substance had begun to form small, closely-packed globules on the blades
of grass and that it had begun to "crystallize".  Mr. Storm states that it
then felt slick (like graphite) when rubbed between the fingers; Mrs. Storm
describes it as a powdery feel.

               (NOTE:  There had been no rain since before the evening of
               1 Sep 52, and there was a hot sun all day on 2 Sep 52.
               However, there was a heavy rainfall during the night of
               2/3 Sep 52).

          g.  During the morning of 3 Sep 52, Mr. Storm reexamined it and
"was surprised to find it there after so much rain".  He describes its
appearance as darker (a slate gray) and still formed in globules on the
grass blades.  It still felt about like graphite, perhaps a bit "thinner"
than the preceding evening.  (Mrs. Storm removed Sample E that morning).

     1.  Subject was the principal in the alleged sighting of an unidentified
flying object in the vicinity of West Palm Beach, Florida on the night of
19 August 1952.  A field investigation of a technical nature has been conducted
by the Air Technical Intelligence Center, but no conclusive results have yet
been obtained.  However, there are indications of a possible hoax, viz. the results
of the FBI lab analysis on Des Vergers' cap (ref your R&R to this office dtd
30 Aug 52) and the actions of Des Vergers subsequent to the alleged sighting.

     2.  A check of subject's Marine Corps personnel records has revealed that
he was given a bad conduct discharge 1 November 1944 following his conviction by
a civil court in Florida for violation of National Motor Vehicle Theft Act.  He
was sentenced to 2½ years in the Federal Reformatory at Chillicothe, Ohio
(Reformatory No. 23542-C).  His Marine Corps medical records were negative as
regards psychiatric indications or treatment.

     3.  It has also been learned, from a source whose reliability cannot be
judged, that subject may have been confined at one time to a mental institution
in the state of New York.

     4.  It is therefore requested that the following information be obtained:

          a.  Any records of psycho-neurotic examination and/or treatment while
confined to the Federal Reformatory at Chillicothe, Ohio.

          b.  Evidence that he was at one time confined to a mental institution in
the state of New York.

July 31, 1952

Major General John Sanford
War Department
Washington, D.C.

Sir:

     General Sanford everybody is taling about the flying saucers
I don't know how I ever got enough nerve to write you but I think it
is my turn now to put in my nickels worth.

     As one serviceman to another I think I can talk frank with you.
I think I know the man who is responsible for the flying saucers, it
is a long story but I will try to make it as brief as possible.

     In 1929 at an inventor's meeting in Long Beach in the Rainbow Pier
I met a man who called himself, at that time, Samuel P. Jones he had a
motor that everyone thought was a fake. He would explain it to you but
no one would believe him but me. So as a dumb cluck I tried to give
the man a helping hand, he said that this motor could be made in any
size or horsepower, could be put in ships, locomotives, cars and
airplanes. At that time I knew a doctor in Long Beach who had a
clinic and a yacht, I took this Jones to this doctor thinking that this
doctor might finance him for a motor for his yacht. After the doctor talked
to the man awhile, the doctor didn't beieve him, though he was nuts, so
then I forgot all about this man Jones until World War II. I met this
same man in the South Pacific and he was a Skipper in the Army Transport
Service. Then after seeing him again and knowing the position he held
I took it for granted that he must be pretty smart, not nuts. I became
very friendly with this man we chummed together for a coule of years
in the South Pacifica and every once in awhile he would tak about his
invention. I asked him if this invention was so good why is it that the
Government wouldn't take it. This is what he told me, that he had tried
to get the Government to take it and they laughed at him and he finally
got an interview with President Roosevelt and the President told him that
at that time he also had an idea before Congress that if it didn't work
out they would all go to the insane asylum. He also told him that his
idean was a thousand years ahead of time.

     Later in 1947 I got a letter from this Jones asking me to come to him,
which I did, in Havre, Montana he had a plane that I would call built with
this motor, this was the most damnable looking plane I have ever seen. It
was made like a saucer, about 17 feet in diameter and it would fly through
the air with a control made from the base of a telephone. This I saw with
my own eyes. He said that it would fly so fast through the air that the
air would melt, and I asked him "how fast will it go", he said actually he
didn't know but would figure it made a speed of 3 to 4000 miles per hour.

        Again, I asked him why he didn't do something about it and he said
it was impossible.  I also, asked him why he didn't patent this machine and
he gave me amny reasons, that each and every part about the machine had already
been invented and it would take a millionaire to procure the patent rights
to this invention.  I also asked him wasn't he afraid that someone would
steal it from him and he told me that the public was funny that they couldn't
see no further than the nose on their face and that if you had a secret that
you wanted to keep to tell everybody and nobody would believe you.

        About three months later I received a letter from this man telling me
that he was ready to make a test, a few days later was the first time I
heard about the flying saucers.  Since that time I have received many letters
from this man Jones.  About three weeks ago I received a letter from him again
telling me that over Baltimore, Washington, Alexander Virginia, etc., that
he was going to let the whole world know that his invention was possible.
Then I went to the American Broadcasting Company, a couple of newspapers
and tried to tell them this story.  They wouldn't even listen to me and it
has happened again.  If this man Jones is not the inventor of the flying
saucer how is it that he knows two or three weeks ahead of time when they are
going to fly?  I think that if you will find this man Jones, I know you will
get this fantastic story straightened out.  His address I do not know but he
writes me to my box in Detroit, Michigan and I receive a letter maybe two
or three weeks later.  When I saw the plane or whatever you want to call it,
in the air, it would go so fast you would hardly see it.  It was round like
a saucer, had a tail like a plane, and when it would sway (as I would say)
in the air sometimes it would look like a pencil, sometimes like a egg, and
again it would look like a balloon so you take it from here.  Use your own
judgment, you have my permission to do anything you want with this letter.
My name is H. D. Springer, I have no permanent address but I live in Detroit,
I am going back east tonight at 9 o'clock P.M.

(Hedo-misaki or Hedo Saki), but on checking his sketch against Inclosure 1, it
appears more probable that the location was actually Oku since there is a lagoon
there about 1 mile wide and a native village at the southern edge of the lagoon,
which seems to check with his sketch.

2.  Request Sgt Guzi be reinterrogated, using Inclosure 1, to determine the
most probable location in question.  In addition an attempt should be made to pin-
point the exact location at which object entered water.

3.  If it transpires that the lagoon at Oku is the proper location, it will
probably be feasible to investigate since the water is very shallow.  Should it
be at Hedo Saki, however, the depth of the water will probably prohibit an inves-
tigation.

4.  Request return of Inclosures 1 and 2 with reply.

MEMORANDUM FOR RECORD

PROBLEM:

     1.  To prepare DF to ATIC.

FACTS AND DISCUSSION:

     2.  T/Sgt Emery Guzi, assigned to WADC at W-P AFB, recently appeared
in person before Project Blue Book personnel at ATIC and volunterred in-
formation concerning the sighting of an u/i flyob on Okinawa in Nov 50.
He stated that the object had fallen into the sea.

     3.  Sgt Guzi pointed out the approximate location on a map and drew
a large scale sketch of the area.

     4.  This information was forwarded to AFOIN-2A2 for the purpose of
determining the feasibility of an attempt to recover or otherwise locate
and examine the object.

     5.  A hydrographic chart of the area was obtained to determine the
soundings and thereby judge the feasibility of an investigation.  However,
it was found that the data reported by Sgt Guzi did not tally with the
hydrographic chart.  ATIC is therefore being requested to reinterrogate
Sgt Guzi in order to resolve these differences.  The attached DF will
accomplish this.

     6.  Subject matter will not be suitable for inclusion in the Daily
Staff Digest.

ACTION RECOMMENDED:

     7.  Approval, signature and dispatch of attached DF.

NASA-UAP-D023, Interview Excerpt with Astronaut Gordon Cooper, 1962

Speaker A: Gordo, you expressed interest at one time in unidentified flying objects, the feeling that there might be something to all these stories. Do you still feel that way?

Speaker B: Well, I, I feel that there have been a large number of fairly well-qualified— or exceptionally well-qualified, I should say— people Who have seen objects that have not, have not had any really logical explanation other than this. I think that maybe in fact each and every one of them does have an explanation, but I think that there are so many possibilities, so many thousands of possibilities of other planets out somewhere in the universe that would have a livable atmosphere. That I would hate to rule out the possibility that maybe there are people or some type of human life on some of these. And if this is the case, then it's not too unfeasible to think that perhaps some of these objects might have been something of this type.

Speaker A: You don't think that the comparatively short step out into space that the Mercury flight will take you on is far enough out to make any observations in this area?

Speaker B: No, I think we're still at a fairly low order of getting out into space when you regard— when you speak of space and being millions of miles involved. We're only getting out 100 miles or so.

Speaker A: What about the so-called Glenn effect, Gordo? The You know, the snowflakes, the fireflies. Mm-hmm. Now, both Schirra and Carpenter seem to feel that it's frost of some nature off of the capsule, but apparently Glenn still sort of casts doubt on that theory.
